weather.gex: Read: the light is RED. SPY at 739.95 sits 2.69% under the 759.85 flip, with the put wall at 730 (1.34% below) and the call wall at 775 (4.74% above), so dealers amplify moves both ways; reclaiming the flip calms the tape and losing 730 removes the cushion. weather.heartbeat: Read: the average stock has beaten the index for 21 days (broadening): +6.27% over 20 days, +2.20% over 60 and +0.79% over the last 5, with confidence 0.75 and a place at the top of its 12-month range, so the phase is late rather than early. The ratio is 2.32% above its 20-day average (0.2890) and 0.99% under its 12-month high (0.2988); a cross under that average would turn it before the label changes.
weather.positioning: Read: trend funds are neutral across 18 markets with none at an extreme (dial 1.00), leaning long currencies (+0.59) and short rates (-0.42) and metals (-0.40). Nearest lines: they turn sellers of soybeans below 1,225.44 (0.11% below) and of small caps below 2,744.39 (0.13% below); for stocks they turn buyers of the S&P 500 above 7,506.05 (0.9% above) and sellers of the Dow below 50,249.09 (2.74% below).
weather.volatility: Read: VIX at 22.91 is higher than 88% of days in two years, so the index is not quiet; VIX/VIX3M is 0.84, down from 1.23 five days ago and under the 1.00 stress line, and the curve is in contango. Single stocks imply 42.77, a gap of 23.47 that is wider than 78% of the past two years and has widened 1.75 points in 20 days, 1.25% under the elevated band at 23.76, but these readings are as of 13 Nov; implied correlation is 16.42.
weather.divergence: Read: Valen counts 0 of 8 market-level warning types fired, and Crown's summary says no warning signs are lit while its count shows 4 with none named. No single one is a reason to sell; they matter when several agree with breadth, and breadth is still broadening.
weather.call: Read: Crown's family is broadening carry, a partial fit at a 1.00x multiplier on the PM's own risk (a reading, not a size): breadth broadening, the stock-level gap normal and trend funds near a low flip are met, while breadth not at an extreme and dealers long gamma both fail. The leading macro story is a dollar squeeze with 93.17% of its conditions met at full coverage, not contested, runner-up liquidity stress. Next tests: retail sales 17 Nov 08:30 ET, FOMC 18 Nov 14:00 ET, jobless claims 19 Nov, ISM 23 Nov, core PCE 25 Nov.
weather.cot: Read: big speculators are crowded long small caps (Russell 2000), the 30-year bond and the 5-year note, and crowded short natural gas and silver. The small-cap crowding is the one that matters for a stock book, as context and not timing, and small caps sit 0.13% above the trend-fund seller line; the report covers 10 Nov.
weather.checklist: Read: net new highs lead (8-day average 64.5 against 42.7 over 20 days), but today's count is not green, the 5-day up/down 4% count is 0.25 against the 1.00 pass, the 10-day count is 0.74 and monthly big risers are 83. Above their 20-day line 42.3%, 50-day 43.7%, 200-day 52.3% and 40-day 45.1%: fewer than half of stocks hold the medium lines, with these counts labelled by the file as US-listed stocks over $2B, not AQE's own list.
weather.turning: Read: stance RISK OFF now against NEUTRAL five days and a month ago; trend DOWNTREND now, CHOP five days ago; VIX/VIX3M 0.84 against 1.23 and 0.80; stocks above their 40-day line 45.1% against 55.4% and 44.6%; SPY -2.09 daily ranges from its 50-day against -1.13 and -0.75. Stocks above their 40-day line clearing 50 or the 5-day count clearing 1.00 (now 0.25) would turn it positive, and the 350 monthly-risers line is a whole-market count (now 83), not a target on AQE's list.
weather.themes: Read: true leaders on both horizons and near their highs are Insurance (+1.99% on the week, +4.71% on the month, 0.94% under its high) and REITs (3.83% under). Oil Services, Enterprise Software and Midstream make the both-horizon list but sit 30%, 14% and 10% under their highs, so they are turns in damaged groups, not leaders; Cloud Computing, Cybersecurity, Gaming Streaming, Agri Commodities and Defense Tech are bounces off the floor.
weather.groups: Read: the turning sectors are Technology (APP, VERX, PCOR), Communication Services (LFTO, LBTYK, LION) and Energy (LNG); the turning themes with two or more strong names are AI Software (APP, SAIL), Social Media (APP, TTD), Enterprise Software (U, BOX) and Gaming Streaming (U, SIRI). Further along and already leading: Consumer Staples, Financials, Utilities, Healthcare, Consumer Discretionary and Real Estate, with Insurance, Travel Leisure and Transport Logistics among the themes; a place to look, not a list to buy.
